title: Cipher key (homophonic alphabet with nomenclature) among the Bellievre papers, undated; names point to the Netherlands affairs of about 1577-78
shelfmark: BnF, Departement des Manuscrits, Francais 15890, f. 326r (Gallica ark:/12148/btv1b105073513, view 659; verso view 660 blank)
note: One oblong leaf, seen at 1600 px on 15 Nov 2026 (openapi.bnf.fr IIIF). No title, date or endorsement on either side. Alphabet A-Z with three signs per letter (invented signs, some figures and letters); 'Doubles' (PP SS MM NN CC DD FF EE TT, two signs each); 'Monosilabes' (car, pour, quand, quel, que, faire, dire, de, la, les, encore, faut); 'Nulles' (four groups); nomenclature down the left margin: Le Roy Catholique, La Royne d'Angleterre, Dom Joan, L'Empereur, L'archiduc, Pays bas, Les Estatz, Le Prince d'Orange, Monseigneur, Le Duc Casimir, Allemans, Francoys, Espagnolz, Italiens, Le Pape, M. de Savoye, Le Roy de Navarre, Huguenotz, Anvers, Le Comte de Lalain, Bruxelles, Mons (my reading; sign values not transcribed). The date is inferred from the names (Don John, the Estates, Orange, Lalaing, Mons, Monseigneur = Anjou), not written on the sheet; it is bound between Polish pieces of 1573 (ff. 324-325) and parchment letters (ff. 327-328). No cipher letter in this key was seen in fr. 15890, 15894, 15897 or 15898. known.py on '15890', 'Dom Joan', 'Comte de Lalain' (15 Nov 2026): no hit. Not checked: Tomokiyo, DECODE, and whether Bellievre's 1578 Netherlands letters (other volumes) use it.
